title: Normalized symmetric monoidal structure on a tensor-compatible reflective subcategory
statement: Let B be a symmetric monoidal category, P an object property, T an endofunctor with natural unit eta, with P(TX) for every X. Suppose precomposition by eta_X gives a bijection Hom(TX,Z) to Hom(X,Z) for each P-local Z, eta is invertible on P-local objects, and T(eta_X tensor 1_W) and T(1_X tensor eta_W) are invertible for all X,W. Then the full P-subcategory admits a symmetric monoidal structure with tensor object T(X tensor Y), tensor morphism T(f tensor g), unit T(1), associator inverse left insertion followed by T(alpha) and right insertion, braiding T(beta), and both unitors inverse unit insertion followed by T of the original unitor and inverse eta on the complete input, exactly as in def-pur-completed-tensor-unit-insertion-data. The reflector is retained as a strong symmetric monoidal functor with cotensorator T(eta_X tensor eta_Y), identity unit, and the braiding equation for these same data.

proof.text:
Proof: lift tensor to the full subcategory by applying T, and take T(1) as unit.
The associator is inverse left insertion, T of the original associator, then right
insertion. The braiding is T of the original braiding. Each unitor is inverse
insertion of the unit followed by T of its original unitor and inverse eta on the
local input. Reflection makes T eta invertible. Naturality of eta identifies both
ways of inserting completion into any parenthesized tensor expression. Tensoring
preserves arrows inverted by T: conjugate with the two insertion isomorphisms and
use naturality. Therefore every iterated insertion is invertible. Precompose the
pentagon, triangle and hexagons with their common iterated insertion; they become T
of the original diagrams. Cancel those isomorphisms. Involutivity follows from T
preserving composition and the original symmetry equation. This also proves the
listed formulas, since they were the chosen constraints. Lean implementation: form the monoidal localization at morphisms inverted by the reflector (Mathlib Localization.Monoidal), then transport its tensor along the adjunction counit using the proved Retensor helper of lem-sfb-braided-sheaf-tensor-generators. The oplax localization identities reduce the transported constraints to the specified formulas. Retain the composite of the monoidal localization and the inverse Retensor equivalence. Naturality of the old cotensorator and the adjunction triangle give its cotensorator T(eta_X tensor eta_Y); the transported unit is identity and its braiding equation follows by composition.
